transcript: This is Harry. This is Hermione. And this is Ron. And they are playing against the giant chessboard in the Philosopher Stone. In this position, they are down a full queen. But thanks to Ron's strategy, they're actually completely winning. We can notice how this bishop, this rook, and this knight are all very close to the white king, and they're about to deliver a checkmate. The only thing that holds the white position together is the evil queen. And that is why Ron decides to distract it by sacrificing the rook. So he plays rook C5 C3. And now the rook is of course going to be captured by the queen very easily. But Ron has seen that this is going to open up an attack of the black bishop on the white king. And now there are two ways to win the game. We can either sacrifice the bishop, distract the queen, and then deliver a checkmate with Ron. But he knows that Harry has to keep going. Not >> me, not Hermione, you. >> And so he decides to sacrifice himself instead. And that is why he plays knight G5 H3. >> Knight to [music] H3. >> And now the king is going to be in check. And there is going to be no square to move to because of the bishop, the rook, and the knight. Forcing the white queen to capture Ron and almost kill him. But now Harry has a path to check the white king. And that is why he moves the bishop from A3 to C5. Now this is not checkmate quite yet. The check can be blocked in only one way by giving up the last piece that was defending everything, the white queen. But now the queen can be taken with bishop C5 E3. And after this move, this is going to be a beautiful >> checkmate. [music]
